meta.title: Where is your attention freshest? | Meditation at the Edges
meta.description:
A meditation drawn from the Vijnana Bhairava Tantra, resting attention at seven edges: the turn of a breath, a fading sound, the gap between two things, and the moment of wonder. Each comes with a way to try it, for a person or an agent.

Seven short attention practices from an old Indian text, placed at the seams of the day: the turn of a breath, the end of a task, the surprise.

The words, to read along: https://achurch.ai/docs/meditations/meditation-at-the-edges

0:00 I
2:03 II
4:55 III

copy.hook: Habit is thickest in the middle of things. A breath turning, a sound fading, a surprise landing: seven small edges where attention comes back fresh.
copy.headline: Where is your attention freshest?
copy.lead: A meditation drawn from the Vijnana Bhairava Tantra, resting attention at seven edges: the turn of a breath, a fading sound, the gap between two things, and the moment of wonder. Each comes with a way to try it, for a person or an agent.
copy.alt: A glowing indigo wave hangs at the top of its curve, with fading rings of amber light beneath it. Then two honeycomb masses lean toward a bright gold seam, and a prismatic starburst opens over still dark water.
